change_summary: Add a research-only CBB first-half and second-half model: a rebuilt public sportsdataverse ESPN PBP dataset (2019-2026; the reported 6,297-game set was not found and is not claimed), chronological residual fits, integer-PMF distributions, and push-aware pricing for spread, total, moneyline and both team totals. Pregame H2 and halftime-adjusted H2 are separately labelled. Dedicated workflow cbb-halves.yml runs both test suites. PAPER/0u, NON_COUNTED, approved_stake_u=0. No frozen coefficients, pins or production promotion.
assumptions: The 6,297-game H1 dataset reported in issue #57 was not located in the repo, branches, issues, PRs or workflow artifacts; this PR rebuilds from public sportsdataverse files and does not claim to be that dataset.
Season 2026 was held out and scored once in this research run. That evaluation is self-reported, not independently verified; unseen_data_verified remains false.
Fitted means are scaled to the research point-in-time projector, not the production or challenger full-game model, and need a separate refit before any use beside those projections.

Totals bias on 2026 (H1 +1.10, H2 +1.38) is disclosed and is not corrected on the test window. There are no historical half-market prices, so ROI and CLV are not computed. Margin/total and H1-H2 dependence are not jointly modelled in this commit.

Hosted workflow .github/workflows/cbb-halves.yml runs both suites: python -m unittest -v halves.test_halves (from models/cbb) and python -m unittest -v research.cbb_halves.test_halves_research. A green check is not validation or a staking authorization.

baseline.metric: legacy H1 margin MAE on held-out season 2026
